reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: §19.1 gives the professional/workmanlike warranty, §19.2 gives 90 days for Deliverables plus term-long conformity for Hosted Services (exceeding the 12-month software preference), §19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law and a no-malicious-code warranty, §19.4 supplies re-perform/repair/replace and refund on failure to cure, and §19.5 expressly prevents the disclaimer from swallowing the express warranties.
No redline or counterparty comment was proposed, which is the correct output for a compliant finding; the rendered paragraphs are unchanged from the originals.

The failed deterministic check is a false negative caused by phrasing: the period is written as 'For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later,' which satisfies the ≥90-day requirement even though the regex expects a numeral or a months/years unit.

The noted softening (malicious code limited to code 'intentionally introduced by Vendor') is a reasonable market-standard concession that does not undercut the preferred position given the non-exclusive remedy stack; declining to redline is defensible.
